subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 30-year-old woman is evaluated for a possible mood episode. Over the past 10 days she has been unusually talkative, needs only 3 hours of sleep, has racing thoughts, is easily distracted, and has started several ambitious projects. Her physician is reviewing the DIG FAST criteria with the team.
question: Which of the following is NOT one of the symptoms included in the DIG FAST mnemonic for a manic episode?
explanation_correct: DIG FAST enumerates the symptoms of a manic episode: Distractibility; Impulsivity/Indiscretion (hedonistic pleasure-seeking without regard to consequences); Grandiosity; Flight of ideas (racing thoughts); increased goal-directed Activity or psychomotor Agitation; decreased need for Sleep; and Talkativeness or pressured speech. Anhedonia, or loss of interest, is a depressive symptom rather than a component of the mania criteria.

explanation_incorrect.A: Increased goal-directed activity or psychomotor agitation is the 'A' in DIG FAST.
explanation_incorrect.B: Impulsivity and indiscretion — seeking pleasure without regard to consequences — is the 'I' in DIG FAST.
explanation_incorrect.C: Talkativeness or pressured speech is the 'T' in DIG FAST.
explanation_incorrect.E: Decreased need for sleep is the 'S' in DIG FAST.

educationalObjective: DIG FAST lists distractibility, impulsivity, grandiosity, flight of ideas, increased activity, decreased sleep, and talkativeness as the symptoms of a manic episode.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 27-year-old man has experienced 9 days of persistently elevated mood and increased energy. During this time he has required only 4 hours of sleep, speaks rapidly, has racing thoughts, and has made several impulsive purchases. His behavior has led to significant conflict at work and he has been suspended.
question: Which of the following best states the diagnostic requirements for a manic episode in this patient?

options.text: At least five symptoms for at least 2 weeks, including depressed mood or anhedonia
Marked functional impairment with at least three symptoms for at least 1 week, or any duration if hospitalization is required
At least four symptoms for at least 4 days without marked impairment
At least two symptoms for at least 6 months
Any single symptom lasting more than 1 day with a clear stressor

explanation_correct: A manic episode is a distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood with increased activity or energy. Diagnosis requires marked functional impairment plus at least three of the DIG FAST symptoms for at least 1 week, or any duration if hospitalization is required. This patient's 9-day episode with decreased sleep, pressured speech, flight of ideas, and impulsivity causing occupational consequences meets criteria for mania.

explanation_incorrect.A: At least five of nine symptoms for 2 weeks describes a major depressive episode, not a manic episode.
explanation_incorrect.C: At least 4 days without marked impairment describes hypomania, which lacks the severity and psychotic features of mania.
explanation_incorrect.D: Two symptoms for at least 6 months does not correspond to mania; mania is an episodic, shorter-duration syndrome.
explanation_incorrect.E: A single symptom lasting over 1 day with a stressor resembles brief psychotic disorder, not a manic episode.

educationalObjective: A manic episode requires markedly impaired functioning plus at least three DIG FAST symptoms for at least 1 week, with the duration requirement waived if hospitalization is needed.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 22-year-old woman has had 4 days of elevated, expansive mood, decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, and grandiosity. Her family reports she has been reckless with money and has not slept at all for 2 nights. She becomes agitated and is brought to the emergency department, where she is admitted involuntarily because she is a danger to herself and others. No hallucinations or delusions are present.
question: Which of the following best characterizes this episode?

options.text: Hypomanic episode, because it has lasted less than 1 week and lacks psychotic features
Major depressive episode with mixed features
Cyclothymic episode, because symptoms are mild and brief
Brief psychotic disorder, because of the acute agitation
Manic episode, because hospitalization is required regardless of duration

explanation_correct: A manic episode requires at least three DIG FAST symptoms for at least 1 week, but the duration requirement is waived if hospitalization is required — mania can be diagnosed at any duration in that setting. Because this patient requires involuntary hospitalization for safety, she meets criteria for a manic episode despite only 4 days of symptoms. Hypomania never necessitates hospitalization and does not cause marked impairment or include psychotic features.

explanation_incorrect.A: Hypomania lasts at least 4 days but does not cause marked impairment or necessitate hospitalization; her need for involuntary admission makes this mania.
explanation_incorrect.B: A major depressive episode requires depressed mood or anhedonia with at least five of nine symptoms for 2 weeks, which is not the presentation here.
explanation_incorrect.C: Cyclothymia is a chronic condition of at least 2 years with mild fluctuations between depressive and hypomanic symptoms, not an acute episode requiring hospitalization.
explanation_incorrect.D: Brief psychotic disorder requires delusions, hallucinations, or disorganized speech/behavior lasting 1 day to 1 month; she has none of these and the picture is one of mood disturbance.

educationalObjective: Mania can be diagnosed at any duration when hospitalization is required; hypomania lasts at least 4 days but never causes marked impairment or requires hospitalization.
